slides.texte_overlay:
How to become effortlessly
good at chatting with anyone
Ask about the best part, not the whole thing. Not "How was your trip?" but "What was the best moment of the trip?" Specific questions get vivid, fun answers.
Talk about the food. At parties, weddings, work events. "Have you tried the little pastries? They're dangerous." Food is the easiest shared topic on earth.
Use their reaction as your guide. If they light up, go deeper. If they go quiet, switch topics. Reading faces keeps conversations easy for everyone.
Have a light opinion ready. "I think breakfast is the best meal, change my mind." A playful opinion invites people to jump in and have fun with you.
Feed your curiosity every day. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and having small stories ready makes chatting with strangers feel effortless.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Having small stories ready makes chatting with strangers effortless.

slides.texte_overlay: Compliment choices, not looks. "Great choice of wine" or "Love that jacket." Complimenting decisions feels genuine and opens an easy conversation.
Introduce yourself again if you forgot their name. "I'm terrible with names, remind me?" Everyone has done it, and honesty makes you more likeable.
